Read his description as a contemporary argument; it is not a court ruling or an official federal report.\n\n“The lapse of time renders it possible to formulate something like a logical statement in regard to the disturbance which began within the corporate limits of the City of Chicago on the 11th of May last, and subsequently extended westward to the Pacific Coast. This disturbance had its origin in a labor strike at the car shops in the town of Pullman, Ill. ... But the Pullman strike culminated in an insurrection which involved the commercial, industrial and transportation interests of two-thirds of the United States ... and required the intervention of the armed forces of the National Government for its suppression.”\n\n“The Pullman Palace Car Company purchased at that point about 500 acres of land, and there erected extensive works for the building of sleeping, parlor and dining-room cars ... The Pullman Company also built at the town of Pullman all the houses needed as homes for its employees ... To this day the Company retains the ownership of this entire property.”\n\n"}}, {"id": "cities", "tag": "CASE 04", "title": "Whose city?", "intro": "Immigration, tenements and competing interpretations of life in industrial cities.", "image": "data:image/jpeg;base64,
